sentence: Compared with last year, the response rate has risen despite a smaller mailing list.

text: Choose the revision that makes the intended comparison explicit: this year's response rate versus last year's response rate. Compared with last year, the response rate has risen despite a smaller mailing list.
options: Compared with last year's mailing list, the response rate has risen.
Compared with last year, the mailing list has produced a higher response rate.
Compared with last year's rate, this year's response rate is higher.
Compared with this year's rate, last year's mailing list was larger.
answer: Compared with last year's rate, this year's response rate is higher.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-c1-2961:A reduced comparative clause needs clearly matched comparison terms
explanation: Both comparison terms are response rates, so the shortened comparative clause attaches to a matching main-clause subject.

rationales.Compared with last year's mailing list,: This explicitly compares a rate with a list rather than with another rate.
rationales.Compared with last year, the mailing lis: This keeps the comparison's two terms implicit and makes the list the grammatical subject.
rationales.Compared with last year's rate, this yea: Both comparison terms are response rates, so the shortened comparative clause attaches to a matching main-clause subject.
rationales.Compared with this year's rate, last yea: This compares a list with a rate and changes the asserted comparison to list size.

sentence: Having worked with the archive for several years, the curator understood why its cataloguing system was difficult to replace.
setupText: Choose the inference supported by the perfect participle phrase.
taskText: Having worked with the archive for several years, the curator understood why its cataloguing system was difficult to replace.
text: Choose the inference supported by the perfect participle phrase. Having worked with the archive for several years, the curator understood why its cataloguing system was difficult to replace.
options: The curator's experience preceded the understanding; continued employment is not ruled out.
The curator had stopped working with the archive before understanding the problem.
The curator understood the problem before gaining experience with the archive.
The curator's years of experience prove that the system could not be replaced.
answer: The curator's experience preceded the understanding; continued employment is not ruled out.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-c1-2962:Perfect participle experience does not necessarily imply a terminated state
explanation: 'Having worked' places relevant experience before the main-clause understanding, but it does not by itself say the association had ended.

rationales.The curator's experience preceded the un: 'Having worked' places relevant experience before the main-clause understanding, but it does not by itself say the association had ended.
rationales.The curator had stopped working with the: Perfect experience does not require the curator to have left the archive.
rationales.The curator understood the problem befor: This reverses the temporal relationship supplied by having worked.
rationales.The curator's years of experience prove: Understood why replacement was difficult does not establish impossibility of replacement.

sentence: Being unfamiliar with the local procurement rules, the consultant hesitated to recommend a supplier.
setupText: Choose the interpretation that preserves the basis of the consultant's hesitation.
taskText: Being unfamiliar with the local procurement rules, the consultant hesitated to recommend a supplier.
text: Choose the interpretation that preserves the basis of the consultant's hesitation. Being unfamiliar with the local procurement rules, the consultant hesitated to recommend a supplier.
options: The consultant had established that the rules prevented a recommendation.
The supplier's unfamiliarity with the rules caused the consultant's hesitation.
The consultant's lack of familiarity with the rules lay behind the hesitation.
The consultant hesitated until new procurement rules were introduced.
answer: The consultant's lack of familiarity with the rules lay behind the hesitation.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-c1-2963:A being-plus-adjective clause attributes an epistemic state to the main subject
explanation: The opening state belongs to the consultant and is presented as the background reason for hesitating.

rationales.The consultant had established that the: Unfamiliarity is a limitation in the consultant's knowledge, not proof that the rules prohibit a recommendation.
rationales.The supplier's unfamiliarity with the ru: The understood subject of being unfamiliar is consultant, not supplier.
rationales.The consultant hesitated until new procu: No rule change or endpoint to the hesitation is given by the state description.
rationales.The consultant's lack of familiarity wit: The opening state belongs to the consultant and is presented as the background reason for hesitating.

sentence: A: Having been approved, the design can enter production. B: If approved, the design can enter production.
setupText: Choose the contrast between the two opening phrases.
taskText: A: Having been approved, the design can enter production. B: If approved, the design can enter production.
text: Choose the contrast between the two opening phrases. A: Having been approved, the design can enter production. B: If approved, the design can enter production.
options: A and B both leave approval entirely hypothetical.
A makes approval a future aim; B reports it as completed.
A says production caused approval; B says approval stopped production.
A presents approval as obtained; B makes production conditional on approval.
answer: A presents approval as obtained; B makes production conditional on approval.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-c1-2964:Perfect passive fact versus conditional passive reduction
explanation: The perfect passive in A asserts prior approval; the reduced if clause in B states a condition without asserting fulfilment.

rationales.A and B both leave approval entirely hyp: Having been approved presents earlier approval as a fact, unlike if approved.
rationales.A presents approval as obtained; B makes: The perfect passive in A asserts prior approval; the reduced if clause in B states a condition without asserting fulfilment.
rationales.A makes approval a future aim; B reports: This reverses the contrast between the factual perfect and the conditional passive phrase.
rationales.A says production caused approval; B say: Neither opening gives the causal or blocking relationship described here.

sentence: The final witness having withdrawn, the panel postponed the hearing.
setupText: Choose the paraphrase that preserves the separate subjects of the two clauses.
taskText: The final witness having withdrawn, the panel postponed the hearing.
text: Choose the paraphrase that preserves the separate subjects of the two clauses. The final witness having withdrawn, the panel postponed the hearing.
options: The final witness postponed the hearing after the panel withdrew.
After the final witness withdrew, the panel postponed the hearing.
The panel withdrew the final witness before attending the hearing.
The panel postponed the hearing so that the final witness could withdraw.
answer: After the final witness withdrew, the panel postponed the hearing.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-c1-2965:An absolute perfect-participle clause has an independent subject
explanation: The opening clause has its own subject, the final witness, while panel remains the actor of postponed.

rationales.The final witness postponed the hearing: This swaps the witness's withdrawal and the panel's postponement.
rationales.The panel withdrew the final witness bef: 'Having withdrawn' is active with 'witness' as its subject; it does not say the panel removed the witness.
rationales.After the final witness withdrew, the pa: The opening clause has its own subject, the final witness, while panel remains the actor of postponed.
rationales.The panel postponed the hearing so that: The withdrawal is presented as already having happened, not a purpose for the postponement.

sentence: All other things being equal, the shorter application process should attract more candidates.
setupText: Choose the role of 'all other things being equal' in the comparison.
taskText: All other things being equal, the shorter application process should attract more candidates.
text: Choose the role of 'all other things being equal' in the comparison. All other things being equal, the shorter application process should attract more candidates.
options: The writer reports that relevant factors were measured and found identical.
The writer holds other relevant factors constant for the comparison.
The writer adjusts candidate totals to make the application processes appear comparable.
The writer assumes that process length has the same effect as the other factors.
answer: The writer holds other relevant factors constant for the comparison.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-c1-2966:A formulaic absolute states a comparison assumption
explanation: 'All other things being equal' sets a comparison condition in which factors other than process length are treated as unchanged.

rationales.The writer holds other relevant factors: 'All other things being equal' sets a comparison condition in which factors other than process length are treated as unchanged.
rationales.The writer reports that relevant factors: The phrase supplies an assumption, not a report that real-world equality was measured.
rationales.The writer adjusts candidate totals to m: Holding other factors constant is not the same as adjusting the outcome totals to make groups look alike.
rationales.The writer assumes that process length h: 'Equal' concerns the values of other factors across the comparison, not equality of their effects with the effect of process length.

sentence: Staffing permitting, the records office will extend its opening hours next month.
setupText: Choose the interpretation of 'staffing permitting'.
taskText: Staffing permitting, the records office will extend its opening hours next month.
text: Choose the interpretation of 'staffing permitting'. Staffing permitting, the records office will extend its opening hours next month.
options: Current staff have formally granted permission for the extension.
The extension will allow staffing levels to be reduced next month.
Staffing arrangements have already been confirmed for longer hours.
Longer opening hours depend on sufficient staffing being available.
answer: Longer opening hours depend on sufficient staffing being available.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-c1-2967:An absolute permitting construction expresses feasibility
explanation: 'Staffing' is the absolute clause's subject; 'permitting' means 'if staffing makes the extension possible'.

rationales.Current staff have formally granted perm: 'Permitting' means making the extension feasible, not employees performing a formal authorization act.
rationales.The extension will allow staffing levels: The staffing condition enables longer hours; the sentence does not propose reducing staffing as their result.
rationales.Staffing arrangements have already been: The conditional absolute leaves adequate staffing as a condition, not a confirmed arrangement.
rationales.Longer opening hours depend on sufficien: 'Staffing' is the absolute clause's subject; 'permitting' means 'if staffing makes the extension possible'.

sentence: Taken together, the interviews and maintenance records suggest that the problem developed gradually.
setupText: Choose the interpretation that preserves the scope of 'taken together'.
taskText: Taken together, the interviews and maintenance records suggest that the problem developed gradually.
text: Choose the interpretation that preserves the scope of 'taken together'. Taken together, the interviews and maintenance records suggest that the problem developed gradually.
options: Each individual interview independently proves a gradual development.
The two types of evidence jointly support a tentative account of gradual development.
The records were collected at the same time as every interview.
The evidence shows that the problem began only after the interviews were completed.
answer: The two types of evidence jointly support a tentative account of gradual development.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-c1-2968:A reduced passive frames joint consideration of multiple evidence types
explanation: 'Taken together' asks the reader to consider interviews and records jointly; 'suggest' keeps the conclusion tentative.

rationales.Each individual interview independently: 'Together' concerns combined consideration, and 'suggest' does not mean each item proves the conclusion independently.
rationales.The two types of evidence jointly suppor: 'Taken together' asks the reader to consider interviews and records jointly; 'suggest' keeps the conclusion tentative.
rationales.The records were collected at the same t: 'Taken' here means 'considered', not necessarily collected simultaneously.
rationales.The evidence shows that the problem bega: The phrase gives a method of considering evidence, not a time when the underlying problem began.

sentence: Viewed solely in terms of cost, the proposal is attractive; its effect on access is less reassuring.
setupText: Choose the reading that preserves the perspective specified by 'viewed solely in terms of cost'.
taskText: Viewed solely in terms of cost, the proposal is attractive; its effect on access is less reassuring.
text: Choose the reading that preserves the perspective specified by 'viewed solely in terms of cost'. Viewed solely in terms of cost, the proposal is attractive; its effect on access is less reassuring.
options: The proposal is attractive overall because access and cost have been assessed together.
The proposal's cost cannot be evaluated until access has been improved.
The proposal is unattractive on cost but attractive on access.
The favourable assessment is limited to cost and does not settle the access question.
answer: The favourable assessment is limited to cost and does not settle the access question.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-c1-2969:A viewpoint participle limits the domain of an evaluation
explanation: The reduced passive phrase specifies the viewpoint under which 'attractive' applies, leaving a different evaluation under access.

rationales.The proposal is attractive overall becau: 'Solely' limits the first assessment to cost; the second clause introduces a less positive access assessment.
rationales.The proposal's cost cannot be evaluated: The sentence makes a cost assessment now rather than postponing it until access improves.
rationales.The favourable assessment is limited to: The reduced passive phrase specifies the viewpoint under which 'attractive' applies, leaving a different evaluation under access.
rationales.The proposal is unattractive on cost but: This reverses both evaluations: cost is attractive, while access is less reassuring.

sentence: Given the uncertainty over the venue, announcing a firm date now would be premature.
setupText: Choose the interpretation of the opening phrase.
taskText: Given the uncertainty over the venue, announcing a firm date now would be premature.
text: Choose the interpretation of the opening phrase. Given the uncertainty over the venue, announcing a firm date now would be premature.
options: Taking the venue uncertainty into account, the writer regards a firm announcement as too early.
The writer treats an early announcement as the source of uncertainty about the venue.
The writer expects a firm date to resolve the uncertainty about the venue.
The writer regards the uncertainty as a reason to announce a flexible date immediately.
answer: Taking the venue uncertainty into account, the writer regards a firm announcement as too early.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-c1-2970:Given introduces a background premise rather than an ordinary giving event
explanation: Given introduces a circumstance used as the basis for judging a firm announcement premature.

rationales.Taking the venue uncertainty into accoun: Given introduces a circumstance used as the basis for judging a firm announcement premature.
rationales.The writer treats an early announcement: This reverses the relationship, making an announcement cause the background uncertainty.
rationales.The writer expects a firm date to resolv: The sentence treats uncertainty as a reason not to announce a firm date now, not as a problem a firm date will solve.
rationales.The writer regards the uncertainty as a: Judging a firm announcement premature does not itself prescribe an immediate flexible-date announcement.

sentence: The editor reviewed the manuscript. After that review, the publisher accepted it.
setupText: Choose the concise version that explicitly keeps the editor as the reviewer and the publisher as the acceptor.
taskText: The editor reviewed the manuscript. After that review, the publisher accepted it.
text: Choose the concise version that explicitly keeps the editor as the reviewer and the publisher as the acceptor. The editor reviewed the manuscript. After that review, the publisher accepted it.

The editor having reviewed the manuscript, the publisher accepted it.

focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-c1-2971:Choosing an explicit-subject absolute to preserve different agents
explanation: The absolute clause explicitly gives reviewing to the editor, while the main clause gives acceptance to the publisher.

rationales.Having reviewed the manuscript, the publ: The shared-subject reading makes the publisher the reviewer, losing the editor's role.
rationales.The editor having reviewed the manuscrip: The absolute clause explicitly gives reviewing to the editor, while the main clause gives acceptance to the publisher.
rationales.The publisher having reviewed the manusc: This swaps the two agents: the publisher reviews and the editor accepts.
rationales.Having accepted the manuscript, the edit: This assigns acceptance to the editor and moves the publisher's review afterward.

sentence: A painting believed to be by a local artist was donated to the gallery.
setupText: Choose the revision that preserves the uncertainty about the painting's creator.

text: Choose the revision that preserves the uncertainty about the painting's creator. A painting believed to be by a local artist was donated to the gallery.
options: A painting thought to be by a local artist was donated to the gallery.
A painting by a local artist was donated to the gallery.

answer: A painting thought to be by a local artist was donated to the gallery.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-c1-2972:A reduced reporting passive retains uncertain attribution
explanation: Thought to be keeps the painting's authorship attributed as a belief rather than established fact.

rationales.A painting by a local artist was donated: Removing believed presents local authorship without the original qualification.
rationales.A painting confirmed to be by a local ar: Confirmed strengthens a belief into an established attribution.
rationales.A local artist donated a painting to the: The original concerns believed authorship, not the donor's identity.
rationales.A painting thought to be by a local arti: Thought to be keeps the painting's authorship attributed as a belief rather than established fact.

sentence: The musician reported to have left the orchestra is still listed on its website.
setupText: Choose the reading that preserves the time relationship inside the shortened description.
taskText: The musician reported to have left the orchestra is still listed on its website.
text: Choose the reading that preserves the time relationship inside the shortened description. The musician reported to have left the orchestra is still listed on its website.
options: The report predicts that the musician will leave after the website is updated.
A report places the departure before the report, while the website still lists the musician.
The website confirms that the musician has already left the orchestra.
The musician reported a future departure by someone else in the orchestra.
answer: A report places the departure before the report, while the website still lists the musician.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-c1-2973:A perfect infinitive inside a reduced reporting passive orders reported time
explanation: 'Reported to have left' uses the perfect infinitive for a departure represented as earlier than the reporting; 'still listed' contrasts with that report.

rationales.A report places the departure before the: 'Reported to have left' uses the perfect infinitive for a departure represented as earlier than the reporting; 'still listed' contrasts with that report.
rationales.The report predicts that the musician wi: To have left is retrospective, not a prediction about leaving after a future update.
rationales.The website confirms that the musician h: The website's listing is the contrasting fact, not confirmation of the reported departure.
rationales.The musician reported a future departure: 'Reported' is passive here; the musician is the reported leaver, not the speaker reporting someone else's plan.

sentence: The revised guide, which is scheduled to be released in October, includes the new walking routes.
setupText: Choose the shortened version that retains an official plan rather than asserting completed publication.
taskText: The revised guide, which is scheduled to be released in October, includes the new walking routes.
text: Choose the shortened version that retains an official plan rather than asserting completed publication. The revised guide, which is scheduled to be released in October, includes the new walking routes.

The revised guide, having been released in October, includes the new walking routes.
The revised guide, scheduled for release in October, includes the new walking routes.

explanation: Scheduled for release retains a planned publication date without treating release as already accomplished.

rationales.The revised guide, scheduled for release: Scheduled for release retains a planned publication date without treating release as already accomplished.

sentence: Not having been consulted about the new route, residents questioned how the decision had been reached.

explanation: The negative perfect passive presents lack of consultation before their questioning of the process.

rationales.Residents had not been consulted before: The negative perfect passive presents lack of consultation before their questioning of the process.

sentence: While broadly supportive of the festival, local traders objected to closing the market square for a full week.

text: Choose the interpretation that keeps the support and reservation attached to the same people. While broadly supportive of the festival, local traders objected to closing the market square for a full week.

The traders supported the festival only while the market square was closed.
The traders withdrew their support for the festival as soon as the closure was announced.

focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-c1-2976:A reduced adjective clause with concessive while
explanation: 'While broadly supportive' means although the traders were supportive overall; the main clause narrows their objection to the closure.

rationales.The festival organizers supported closin: The supportive subject is 'local traders', not the festival organizers.
rationales.The traders supported the festival only: While is concessive here, not a limit on the time during which traders offered support.
rationales.The traders withdrew their support for t: A specific objection does not establish that broad support was withdrawn.
rationales.The traders supported the festival in ge: 'While broadly supportive' means although the traders were supportive overall; the main clause narrows their objection to the closure.

sentence: The timetable was revised at short notice, leaving several volunteers unable to attend.
setupText: Choose the claim supported by the final participle clause.
taskText: The timetable was revised at short notice, leaving several volunteers unable to attend.
text: Choose the claim supported by the final participle clause. The timetable was revised at short notice, leaving several volunteers unable to attend.

Volunteers' inability to attend was the stated reason for revising the timetable.

focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-c1-2977:A result participle does not establish intention or prior cause
explanation: Leaving links volunteers' inability to attend to the revision as its consequence.

rationales.The revision had the consequence that so: Leaving links volunteers' inability to attend to the revision as its consequence.
rationales.The timetable was revised in order to pr: A resulting problem is not necessarily the purpose of the revision; no exclusion motive is stated.
rationales.Volunteers' inability to attend was the: This reverses the relation by making the consequence the prior reason for revision.
rationales.The volunteers who attended were respons: The final clause describes affected volunteers, not who revised the timetable.

sentence: The conservator examined documents from the archive damaged in the flood.

explanation: Placing flood-damaged directly before documents removes the competing attachment to archive.

rationales.The conservator examined flood-damaged d: Placing flood-damaged directly before documents removes the competing attachment to archive.
rationales.The conservator examined the archive dam: This assigns damage to the archive and makes it an additional examined object.

sentence: Despite having been advised not to repaint the frame, the owner chose a different colour.

explanation: The negative advice concerns repainting, and despite contrasts it with choosing a new colour; actual repainting is not asserted.

rationales.The owner had received no advice about r: The perfect passive asserts that advice was given; not applies to repaint, not to receipt of advice.
rationales.The owner received advice against repain: The negative advice concerns repainting, and despite contrasts it with choosing a new colour; actual repainting is not asserted.
rationales.The owner advised the restorer against c: The owner is the recipient of the advice, not the adviser.
rationales.The owner accepted advice to repaint and: The advice was not to repaint, rather than advice to repaint that the owner followed.

sentence: Reading the draft on the train, Sora noticed that two sections gave different dates.

explanation: While makes the overlapping reading explicit while leaving completion unstated.

rationales.While reading the draft on the train, So: While makes the overlapping reading explicit while leaving completion unstated.
